normativeLanguage: MUST, MUST NOT, REQUIRED, SHALL, SHALL NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, MAY are normative. Every object is closed: keys not listed by the selected schema are forbidden.
purpose: Authenticated product-to-orchestrator conversion of product lifecycle evidence into the single-use acquire/consume/assert/release lease and pin required by the product HostedApprovalRuntimeAdmissionPublisher.
nonGoals: This is not the five-operation HostedApprovalWire schema v4 decision/ingress protocol.
This is not the OpenCode hosted-approval v2 HTTP provider protocol.
The release operation releases only an in-process transition pin; it is not a software, artifact, supply-chain, notarization, or external release signature.

wire.transport: one request and one response per privately owned Unix-domain stream-socket connection
wire.socket: the exact HostedControlBootstrap socketPath and published socket identity for the team owner; no route catalog, alternate socket, TCP fallback, or cross-team multiplexing
wire.frame: canonical UTF-8 JSON object followed by exactly one LF byte
wire.proofInput: UTF8(domain) || 0x00 || UTF8(direction) || 0x00 || exact canonical unsigned-envelope bytes
wire.unsignedEnvelope: the complete top-level object with the final ownerProof member removed and the preceding comma removed; the LF delimiter is never authenticated
wire.keySource: the same exact 32 raw secret bytes admitted as HostedControlBootstrapAdmission.secret from the authenticated one-use descriptor bootstrap frame; the product launcher MUST retain one protected in-memory copy for this client and the orchestrator MUST use its admitted copy
keySourceProhibitions: no key derivation from ownerProof, proofKeyId, owner token, digest, path, or identifier
legacy secretFile startup does not enable HostedApprovalTransitionWire v1

canonicalJson.serializer: ECMAScript JSON.stringify semantics over a validated value, with schema key order and dictionary sorting below
canonicalJson.topLevelDelimiter: one 0x0a byte after the JSON value
forbiddenInsideFrame: duplicate object keys at any depth, including escaped spellings that decode to the same key
NaN, Infinity, -Infinity, negative zero, fractions, unsafe integers
canonicalJson.strings: JSON.stringify escaping is canonical: quotation mark, reverse solidus, and U+0000 through U+001F use JSON.stringify spelling; other valid Unicode scalar values are emitted as their UTF-8 characters
canonicalJson.numbers: decimal JSON.stringify representation of integers in [0, 9007199254740991], with field-specific positive minima
canonicalJson.arrays: preserve schema-defined order; routes MUST be strictly ascending by routeId using JavaScript UTF-16 code-unit comparison
canonicalJson.dictionaries: memberIdsByName and actorMembers keys MUST be strictly ascending using JavaScript UTF-16 code-unit comparison

digestRules.requestDigest: lowercase SHA-256 of the exact unsigned request envelope bytes
digestRules.projectionDigest: lowercase SHA-256 of canonical productProjection JSON bytes
digestRules.bindingDigest: lowercase SHA-256 of canonical binding JSON bytes
digestRules.prefixRule: requestDigest, projectionDigest, bindingDigest, declaredRootHash, sessionRecordFingerprint, and liveEffectFingerprint have no prefix; approvalDigest, expectedInstalledArtifactDigest, and openCodeArtifactDigest include the literal sha256: prefix

fields.operation: one of acquire, consume, assert, release
fields.payload: the exact request payload selected by operation

fields.requestDigest: hexSha256 of the exact unsigned request
fields.payload: the exact success payload selected by operation

fields.requestDigest: hexSha256 of the exact unsigned request

consumeSuccessPayload.bindingDigest: hexSha256 of canonical returned binding bytes and exact request bindingDigest
consumeSuccessPayload.binding: fresh authoritative reread, canonical and byte-digest equal to the acquire binding

assertSuccessPayload.reason: null iff current is true; otherwise one of expired, released, fenced, owner_restarted, binding_changed, socket_changed, process_changed, client_changed

releaseSuccessPayload.releasedAtMs: safeNonNegativeInteger; stable tombstone time returned unchanged on every idempotent replay

fields.teamName: teamName; lookup key only and never authority by itself
fields.expectedInstalledArtifactDigest: prefixedSha256 obtained by a fresh product-installed-binary verifier read; never supplied by the orchestrator
fields.stableAuthority: OuterAuthority from the product launch/admission projection
fields.expectedOwner: Owner expected by the product launch/readiness projection
fields.clientProcessIdentity: ProcessIdentity of the product process that opens this UDS connection

crossChecks: expectedInstalledArtifactDigest is freshly reread by the product again at every publisher fence; the request value does not replace those local rereads
clientProcessIdentity must match kernel peer credentials and a fresh process-start identity read
binding.outerAuthority is deeply equal to productProjection.stableAuthority
binding.owner is deeply equal to productProjection.expectedOwner
memberIdsByName and actorMembers have equal counts and exactly the same unique memberId value set
every route authority deploymentId and teamId equal outerAuthority
every route scope workspaceId, teamId, and restoreGeneration equal outerAuthority
each openCodeBinding planGeneration, credentialGeneration, credentialId, runtimeInstanceId, and deliveryOwnerId equals the corresponding route authority field
routeId and authority.sessionId are independently unique
providerId is opencode and toolApprovalMode is manual

processStartIdentityAlgorithm.linuxSource: proc:<field22>, where field22 is the decimal kernel start tick parsed from /proc/<pid>/stat after the final ')' command delimiter
processStartIdentityAlgorithm.darwinSource: ps:<lstart>, where lstart is the nonempty trimmed output of ps -o lstart= -p <pid>
processStartIdentityAlgorithm.failure: no identity is admitted; no time/uptime approximation is allowed by this wire

productBeforeConnect: lstat expectedOwner.socketPath: it is a socket, not a symlink, mode exactly 0600, uid is the product effective uid, and dev/inode/uid/gid/mode equal expectedOwner.socketIdentity
open and pin the canonical parent directory; it is a real directory, not a symlink, owner-controlled, and its dev/inode stays unchanged
connect only to that path and obtain server peer credentials; peer pid and uid must equal expectedOwner.processIdentity.pid and socket uid
repeat socket-path and server process-start checks after connect, before every write, and after every response
orchestratorOnEveryRequest: the listening socket and pinned parent still have the exact admitted identities and private modes
kernel peer uid equals the orchestrator effective uid
kernel peer pid equals productProjection.clientProcessIdentity.pid on acquire and the pid stored in the lease thereafter
fresh peer process-start identity equals the stored clientProcessIdentity.startIdentity
owner descriptor guard, ownerAuthority, ownerGeneration, ownerSessionId, owner socket identity, and owner process identity are current
identityChecks.unsupportedPlatformRule: If kernel peer pid, uid, and process start cannot all be proved, the wire is unavailable and performs no acquire.

deadlines.clock: Unix epoch milliseconds from a monotonic-deadline wrapper; wall-clock rollback never extends an admitted deadline
rules: deadlineAtMs must be greater than receipt time and no farther in the future than the operation maximum
the server must finish durable state change and write the complete response before deadlineAtMs
an acquired lease expiry is fixed at durable acquire commit time plus 10000 ms
a pin expiry is fixed at durable consume commit time plus 30000 ms and assert does not extend it
expiration fences the lease before replying
timeouts and disconnects are safe to retry only under the idempotency rules

identifierSemantics.transitionId: Product-generated cryptographically random 128-bit lowercase hex ID for one logical lifecycle publication attempt. It is stable across permitted retries, never reused for another team, lifecycle value, projection, or owner session, and is not an approvalId, requestId, deliveryRef, or external release identifier.
identifierSemantics.leaseId: Orchestrator-generated cryptographically random 128-bit lowercase hex capability handle. It is globally unique, bound to exactly one transitionId, teamId, generation, projectionDigest, bindingDigest, client process identity, and owner identity, and is never accepted as authentication without the frame HMAC.
identifierSemantics.sequence: Per-transition positive request sequence. acquire is exactly 1. The first state-changing request after a successful operation is previous committed sequence plus 1. Repeating the exact same sequence and requestDigest is a replay; any changed bytes at an existing sequence or any gap is rejected.
identifierSemantics.generation: Orchestrator-owned durable per-team authoritative-binding generation. It advances monotonically and is never reused when the canonical binding changes or the owner process restarts. Concurrent acquired leases over the same exact binding may share a generation. It is not ownerGeneration, approvalGeneration, planGeneration, credentialGeneration, restoreGeneration, mountGeneration, authorityGeneration, admissionGeneration, writer-fence generation, or WAL revision.
identifierSemantics.ownerGeneration: Orchestrator owner authority epoch and product lifecycle input. It must match in lifecycle, expectedOwner, and binding.owner.
identifierSemantics.approvalGeneration: Product-owned admission high-water used only by restart_required and active lifecycle states. It is not allocated or modified by this wire.

transitions.effect: durably record transition, lease, generation, both digests, immutable binding, identities, sequence 1, expiry, request digest, and exact response before replying
obtain the exclusive per-team binding-change pin, fresh-reread all binding sources and identities, prove both digests unchanged, durably mark consumed, then return the fresh binding
freshly prove the exclusive pin, generation, binding sources, socket, both processes, and owner descriptor; current=true only if every check succeeds
durably tombstone, release the exclusive pin, and return the stable releasedAtMs
allowed cleanup of an unconsumed lease; durably tombstone without creating a pin
fence first and release any pin

transitions.event: binding, socket, owner, or process drift
transitions.effect: fence first and release any pin; assert returns current=false with the exact reason
recovery fences all nonterminal leases before readiness and advances generation

illegalOperationOrder: any operation after a terminal tombstone except an exact replay or release lookup
stateMachine.assertFalseRule: current=false is a successful, authenticated terminal observation, not a retryable transport error. The product must ensure admission absence and must not continue publication.

minimumFields: requestDigest and exact response for every retained sequence
tombstones.eviction: Only terminal tombstones older than 86400000 ms may be evicted, oldest terminalAtMs first. Active records are never evicted. If 4096 retained tombstones leave no legal slot, acquire returns TOMBSTONE_CAPACITY and changes no state.

idempotency.exactReplay: If requestDigest matches the retained digest at that sequence, perform this lookup before the deadline check and return the byte-identical retained response even when the original deadline has since elapsed, including original timestamps, leaseId, generation, requestDigest, error, HMAC, and LF; perform no state change and no new binding read.
idempotency.changedReplay: Same transitionId and sequence with a different requestDigest is TRANSITION_CONFLICT.
idempotency.sameTransitionNextSequence: Allowed only for the operation legal in the current state and with all lease, generation, projection, and binding fields exact. After a retained retryable same_operation error, the immediately next sequence may repeat that same operation with the same payload identity and a new deadline; acquire compares productProjection/projectionDigest, and other operations compare every payload field.
idempotency.lostResponse: The client retries the same logical operation with the same transitionId, same sequence, same deadlineAtMs, and byte-identical frame. A retained exact replay returns its cached response even after that request deadline. A new sequence is used only after the client actually receives a retryable same_operation error; state lookup and payload equality prevent a second effect.
idempotency.releaseReplay: Always returns the original releasedAtMs; it never signs, publishes, deletes, or releases a software artifact.

orchestratorRecovery: Before transition-wire readiness, exclusively open the private durable ledger, validate canonical bytes and exact schema, and fail closed on corruption.
Convert every acquired or pinned record from the prior process identity to restart_tombstone, release no assumed-surviving userspace lock, and durably fsync the result.
Advance the per-team binding-generation high-water at least once; no pre-restart generation can become current.
Do not reconstruct a live pin and do not call provider APIs during recovery.
productRecovery: No lease or pin survives product process restart.
Revoke or prove absence of hosted-approval-runtime-admission.v1.json before starting a new transition if the prior publication did not reach a proved active state.
Use a new transitionId after either peer process restarts or after any new_transition error.
restartAndFencing.exclusivePin: consume and every orchestrator mutation capable of changing outerAuthority, routes, memberIdsByName, actorMembers, owner, capability, installed OpenCode session/config/process evidence, or their backing records use the same per-team exclusive serialization primitive. Binding change waits for release/expiry; if it cannot wait, it first fences the pin and the product publication fails closed.
proofPoints: consume fresh reread after pin acquisition
assert after rename and directory fsync
restartAndFencing.productArtifactFence: The product independently rereads expectedInstalledArtifactDigest at the same proof points. A matching wire field alone is insufficient.
restartAndFencing.failureRule: Any lost response, HMAC failure, socket substitution, peer-process mismatch, assert false, binding mismatch, pin expiry, or release uncertainty makes the product transition unavailable/revoked; it never preserves a possibly stale admission as active.

errors.signedErrorEligibility: Only an envelope with valid framing, fatal UTF-8, canonical proof-last structure, recognizable common fields, and a valid HMAC may receive a signed error. Otherwise the server closes the connection without bytes and without state change.

retryRules.same_operation: retry the same transition and logical operation under idempotency rules; use exact replay while its signed deadline remains live, otherwise use the next sequence with a new valid deadline
retryRules.new_transition: first ensure product admission absence, discard the lease, refresh owner/readiness/product projections, and generate a new transitionId
retryRules.never: do not automatically retry; treat as contract/configuration fault

productFiles.access: product writes/replaces/unlinks; orchestrator reads only after its normal approval-owner admission boundary

orchestratorFiles.access: orchestrator only; durable generation, transitions, cached responses, and tombstones
orchestrator only; exclusive lock serialized with all binding-source mutation
orchestrator only; not the transition ledger

goldenVectors.encoding: Every canonicalUnsigned string is the exact UTF-8 unsigned-envelope byte sequence. It is canonical except where a negative vector explicitly says the bytes are intentionally noncanonical. Append ,"ownerProof":"<expectedHmacSha256>" before the final } and then one LF to form a signed frame.
goldenVectors.testOnlyKeyWarning: test only; MUST NOT be used outside deterministic contract tests

vectors.construction: 8388608 ASCII x bytes followed by one LF, for a total of 8388609 bytes
vectors.expected: destroy connection immediately when byte count becomes 8388609; do not parse, authenticate, respond, allocate a transition, or retain the bytes
accept response, fence transition, revoke product admission, never publish

implementationChecklist: Both repositories pin this JSON artifact SHA-256 in contract tests without importing runtime code across repositories.

Both codecs reject noncanonical key order, duplicate keys at every depth, trailing commas/whitespace, BOM, invalid UTF-8, unpaired surrogates, unsafe numbers, additional fields, proof-not-last, and frames over 8388608 bytes including LF.
Both codecs reproduce every golden unsigned SHA-256 and HMAC with the explicit test-only key.
Product retains the descriptor-bootstrap secret only in protected memory and zeroes it on owner loss/shutdown.
Product implements exact socket lstat/parent pin/peer credential/process-start checks and never falls back to another socket or team.
Orchestrator implements reciprocal peer checks and revalidates socket, descriptor, and both process identities on every operation.
Orchestrator builds all binding fields from authoritative owner/session/capability sources and enforces every cross-check and limit.
Product builds all productProjection fields from launch/lifecycle/installed-artifact sources and freshly rereads the artifact digest at every publisher fence.
Durable transition ledger atomically records generation, sequence, cached response, expiry, and tombstone before response write, with file and parent fsync.
Exact replays return byte-identical cached responses; changed replays, gaps, and illegal operation order produce the specified codes.
consume shares an exclusive serialization primitive with every binding-source mutation; assert proof points surround reserve, rename, and fsync; release is in finally.
Restart recovery fences all nonterminal leases, advances generation, performs no provider calls, and finishes before readiness.
Product maps assert current=false, identity drift, restart, expiry, HMAC loss, and uncertain settlement to awaited admission revocation/absence.
Product alone writes admission/state files; orchestrator alone writes lease and owner WAL files; permissions and no-follow/canonical-parent checks are tested.

Integration tests cover two-generation provisioning/restart_required/active flow, binding rotation, owner restart, PID reuse, socket substitution, deadline boundaries, tombstone capacity, and 8MiB exactly/plus-one framing.
No release operation, field, proof, key, or test is wired to external software release signing, artifact notarization, or distribution metadata.
